items.question: What is MotoVault?
items.answer: MotoVault is a motorcycle management app built for riders. Track maintenance tasks with smart reminders, log every expense (fuel, gear, parts), record your rides, and diagnose issues with AI photo analysis — all in one app.

items.question: Is MotoVault free?
items.answer: Yes! MotoVault offers a free tier that includes maintenance tracking with smart reminders, one bike in your garage, expense logging, and limited AI diagnostics. For unlimited bikes, full expense analytics, unlimited AI diagnostics, and all learning content, you can upgrade to MotoVault Pro within the app.

items.question: What motorcycles are supported?
items.answer: MotoVault supports all motorcycle makes and models. Our database uses the official NHTSA vehicle data, covering thousands of makes and models across all years. Simply search for your bike when adding it to your garage.

items.question: How does AI diagnostics work?
items.answer: Take a photo of any part of your motorcycle and describe the issue. Our AI analyzes the image and provides a diagnostic assessment with severity ratings — from critical issues that need immediate attention to minor maintenance suggestions.

items.question: Is my data safe?
items.answer: Your data is encrypted and stored securely. We use platform-native security on your device, and all communication is encrypted. We never share your personal info or bike data with anyone.

items.question: What's included in MotoVault Pro?
items.answer: MotoVault Pro unlocks unlimited bikes, full expense analytics with cost-per-mile, unlimited AI diagnostics, access to all lessons and courses, priority support, and exclusive content. You can subscribe monthly or yearly from within the app.

items.question: What is the best motorcycle maintenance app?
items.answer: MotoVault is the most complete motorcycle maintenance app available in 2026. It combines maintenance tracking with service reminders, expense logging, ride recording, AI-powered diagnostics, and structured learning paths — all in one app. Other popular options include MotorManage (manufacturer-spec schedules), Moto Shed (simple one-time purchase logger), and RideLog (iOS-only with automatic ride detection). MotoVault is the only app that covers all five categories.

items.question: How is MotoVault different from other motorcycle apps?
items.answer: Most motorcycle apps focus on one thing: REVER and Calimoto do route planning, MotorManage and Moto Shed do maintenance logging, MotoScan does OBD diagnostics. MotoVault is the only motorcycle app that combines maintenance tracking, expense management, ride logging, AI-powered photo diagnostics (no hardware needed), and structured learning content in a single platform. It works on both iOS and Android and supports all motorcycle makes and models.

Privacy.title: Privacy Policy
Privacy.infoCollect: MotoVault collects the following types of information: (1) Authentication Data — email address and name through Supabase Auth (Google, Apple, or email sign-in); (2) Motorcycle Data — make, model, year, maintenance history, and service records you add to your garage; (3) Diagnostic Images — photos you upload for AI analysis; these are processed in real-time and deleted after analysis; (4) Usage Analytics — app interactions and feature usage tracked via PostHog to improve services; (5) Crash Reports — technical error data collected by Sentry to diagnose and fix issues; (6) Device Information — basic device identifiers for authentication and app functionality.
Privacy.howWeUse: Your information is used to: (1) Provide core services — account management, garage functionality, AI diagnostics, and learning modules; (2) Improve products — analyze usage patterns to enhance features and user experience; (3) Prevent fraud and security threats — detect unauthorized access and suspicious activity; (4) Comply with legal obligations — respond to lawful requests and enforce our terms; (5) Send service updates — notifications about account changes, new features, and important policy updates. We do not sell, rent, or share your personal information with third parties for marketing purposes.
Privacy.thirdParty: MotoVault relies on the following trusted services: (1) Supabase — authentication, database, and user management with enterprise encryption; (2) Anthropic Claude AI — processes diagnostic images and generates analysis (images are not retained); (3) Sentry — monitors application errors and crashes to improve stability; (4) PostHog — tracks feature usage and engagement to optimize the user experience; (5) NHTSA — provides motorcycle make/model/year data (no personal data shared). Each service provider maintains strict data protection practices and complies with applicable privacy laws.
Privacy.dataRetention: We retain your data only as long as necessary: (1) Account data — retained while your account is active and for 90 days after deletion; (2) Diagnostic images — processed and deleted within hours of upload; we do not store images permanently; (3) Usage analytics — retained for 6 months to identify trends; (4) Crash reports — retained for 30 days to diagnose and fix issues; (5) Backup copies — maintained for 30 days for disaster recovery. You can request permanent deletion of your account and associated data at any time.
Privacy.security: MotoVault implements enterprise-grade security measures: (1) Encryption in transit — all data transmitted over HTTPS/TLS; (2) Encryption at rest — sensitive data encrypted in databases; (3) Authentication — secure JWT tokens validated locally without network exposure; (4) Secure storage — authentication tokens stored in platform-native secure storage on mobile, never in AsyncStorage; (5) Access controls — strict role-based access policies for staff; (6) Regular audits — security practices regularly reviewed and updated. While we employ strong protections, no system is 100% secure; we maintain appropriate insurance and incident response procedures.
Privacy.yourRights: Under GDPR (EU residents) and CCPA (California residents), you have the following rights: (1) Right to Access — request a copy of your personal data; (2) Right to Rectification — correct inaccurate information; (3) Right to Erasure — request deletion of your data (right to be forgotten); (4) Right to Restrict Processing — limit how your data is used; (5) Right to Data Portability — receive your data in a structured, portable format; (6) Right to Object — opt out of certain processing, including marketing and analytics; (7) Right to Withdraw Consent — revoke any prior consent for specific data uses. California residents also have the right to know whether their data is sold and to request deletion of data collected. To exercise any of these rights, contact support@motovault.app with specific details of your request and verification of identity.
Privacy.childrenPrivacy: MotoVault is not intended for users under 13 years of age. We do not knowingly collect personal information from children under 13. If we learn that we have collected such information, we will delete it immediately and take steps to prevent further collection. Parents or guardians who believe we have collected data from a child should contact us immediately at support@motovault.app.
Privacy.internationalTransfers: MotoVault operates globally. Your data may be transferred to, stored in, and processed in countries other than your country of residence, including the United States. These countries may not provide the same level of data protection as your home country. By using MotoVault, you consent to the transfer of your information to countries outside your country of residence for the purposes described in this policy. We implement standard contractual clauses and other mechanisms to ensure adequate protection for international data transfers.
Privacy.accountDeletion: You can delete your account and request permanent removal of your personal data at any time. To do so: (1) Log into your MotoVault account; (2) Navigate to Settings > Privacy & Data; (3) Select 'Delete My Account'; (4) Confirm the deletion (this action is irreversible). Your email, personal information, and garage data will be permanently deleted from our systems within 90 days. Some data may be retained longer if required by law or in anonymized/aggregated form for analytics.
Privacy.changes: MotoVault may update this Privacy Policy to reflect new features, services, or legal requirements. We will notify you of material changes by email or by displaying a prominent notice on our website. Your continued use of MotoVault after changes become effective constitutes acceptance of the updated policy. faq.question: How does AI motorcycle diagnostics work without OBD?
faq.answer: MotoVault uses advanced photo-based diagnosis powered by AI. Simply take a photo of the issue or describe your symptoms, and our AI analyzes the image to identify components, detect wear patterns, spot fluid leaks, and assess damage severity. Unlike OBD scanners that read error codes through a port, MotoVault uses visual recognition — meaning it works on every motorcycle regardless of age or make, with no adapters or cables required.

faq.question: What motorcycle problems can MotoVault diagnose?
faq.answer: MotoVault can diagnose a wide range of issues including engine problems (overheating, oil leaks, unusual noises), electrical system faults (dead batteries, faulty wiring, blown fuses), brake wear and pad thickness, tire condition and tread depth, suspension leaks and sag, chain tension and sprocket wear, fluid leaks and contamination, corrosion and body damage, and dashboard warning lights. Each diagnosis includes a severity rating so you know what needs immediate attention.

faq.question: Is AI motorcycle diagnostics accurate?
faq.answer: MotoVault's AI provides highly accurate initial assessments based on visual analysis and cross-referencing thousands of known issues. Each diagnosis comes with a confidence score indicating the AI's certainty level. For critical safety issues like brake failure or structural damage, we always recommend confirming with a qualified mechanic. Think of MotoVault as a knowledgeable riding companion that helps you understand problems — not a replacement for professional service when it matters most.

faq.question: Do I need special equipment for AI diagnostics?
faq.answer: No special equipment is needed — just your smartphone camera. MotoVault is designed to work with the camera already in your pocket. Take a clear, well-lit photo of the part or issue, and the AI handles the rest. No OBD adapters, no Bluetooth dongles, no proprietary tools. This makes MotoVault accessible to every rider regardless of technical experience or budget.

faq.question: How is MotoVault different from OBD2 scanners?
faq.answer: Traditional OBD2 scanners only work on bikes with an OBD port (mostly newer models), require a physical adapter, and can only read stored error codes. MotoVault works on any motorcycle — vintage, modern, carbureted, or fuel-injected — because it uses visual AI analysis instead of electronic port reading. It can identify problems that OBD scanners miss entirely, such as physical wear, corrosion, fluid leaks, and tire condition. Plus, MotoVault provides plain-language explanations instead of cryptic error codes.

FeaturesDiagnostics.longFormTitle: How AI Motorcycle Diagnostics Works: A Complete Guide
FeaturesDiagnostics.longFormIntro: Motorcycle diagnostics has traditionally been the domain of experienced mechanics with specialized tools. MotoVault changes that by putting AI-powered diagnostic capabilities directly in your pocket. Whether you are a seasoned rider who has been wrenching for decades or a new rider who just bought their first bike, MotoVault's AI diagnostics helps you understand what is happening with your motorcycle — quickly, accurately, and without expensive equipment.
FeaturesDiagnostics.longFormHowTitle: From Photo to Diagnosis in Seconds
FeaturesDiagnostics.longFormHow: The process is straightforward. Open MotoVault, point your camera at the part or issue you want analyzed, and snap a photo. You can also describe symptoms you have noticed — unusual sounds, vibrations, or changes in performance. Our AI engine processes the image using advanced computer vision, identifying components, detecting wear patterns, and cross-referencing known issues for your specific motorcycle make, model, and year. Within seconds, you receive a detailed diagnosis that includes what the issue is, how severe it is on a scale from minor to critical, recommended next steps, and estimated repair costs. The AI draws from a vast database of motorcycle-specific knowledge covering over 18,000 bike models.
FeaturesDiagnostics.longFormExamples: Riders use MotoVault diagnostics in countless real-world scenarios. A rider notices a puddle under their parked bike — they snap a photo and MotoVault identifies it as a coolant leak from the water pump seal, rated as moderate severity with a recommendation to replace the seal before the next long ride. Another rider sees a dashboard warning light they do not recognize — a quick photo identifies it as a lean fuel mixture indicator, likely caused by a dirty air filter. A new rider inspecting their used purchase photographs the chain — MotoVault detects excessive stretch and worn sprocket teeth, recommending a full chain and sprocket replacement. These are the kinds of everyday situations where having an AI mechanic in your pocket saves time, money, and prevents breakdowns.
FeaturesDiagnostics.longFormComparison: Traditional motorcycle diagnostics relies on OBD2 scanners (limited to newer bikes with compatible ports), multimeters for electrical testing, and the trained eye of an experienced mechanic. MotoVault does not replace these tools entirely — instead, it complements them by providing an accessible first line of diagnosis. Where an OBD scanner reads stored error codes, MotoVault visually identifies problems that have no error code: worn brake pads, corroded terminals, leaking fork seals, or a chain that needs adjustment. Where a mechanic uses years of experience to spot issues, MotoVault uses AI trained on thousands of motorcycle problems to give you a similar level of insight. The result is faster, more informed decisions about your motorcycle's health — whether you fix it yourself or take it to a shop with a clear understanding of the problem.

VsScenic.description: MotoVault vs Scenic comparison — cross-platform maintenance, expenses, and AI diagnostics vs Scenic's iOS-only curvy-road planner. See which fits your ride.
VsScenic.heroSubtitle: Scenic is a beautifully crafted iOS-only curvy-road planner. MotoVault runs on both iOS and Android and covers maintenance, expenses, diagnostics, and learning — the half of ownership Scenic doesn't touch.
VsScenic.testingPreamble: Tested April 2026 on an iPhone 15 Pro running iOS 18.3, paired with an Apple Watch Series 9, alongside MotoVault 1.4.x on the same device and on a Pixel 8 running Android 15. We planned and rode two curvy day loops with Scenic's route engine, then tracked fuel, service, and ride logs in MotoVault. Scenic's route rendering and waypoint editing are genuinely gorgeous — but the iOS-only reality kept coming up the moment we tried to share anything with an Android-riding friend. Everything below is first-hand; we don't repeat marketing copy.
VsScenic.pricingRow0Notes: Scenic is a one-time App Store purchase; there is no free version of the app.
VsScenic.pricingRow1Notes: Scenic is refreshingly subscription-free; map packs are sold as one-off in-app purchases.
VsScenic.pricingRow2Notes: Scenic has no trial — you buy the app outright on the App Store.
VsScenic.parityRow0Notes: Scenic has no Android build and none has ever been announced.
VsScenic.parityRow1Mv: Partial — multi-day trips with typed waypoints
VsScenic.parityRow1Notes: Scenic's twisty-road routing is arguably the best we've used on any platform.
VsScenic.parityRow2Notes: Scenic's offline story is a core strength; MotoVault is catching up.
VsScenic.parityRow3Notes: Scenic's tactile waypoint editing is one of its standout design touches.
VsScenic.parityRow4Notes: Scenic's Apple Watch integration is uniquely good for iOS riders.
VsScenic.parityRow5Mv: Yes — service history, mileage + time reminders
VsScenic.parityRow5Notes: Scenic doesn't touch maintenance at all.
VsScenic.parityRow8Notes: Scenic is purely a route planner.
VsScenic.parityRow9Notes: Scenic is a solo planning tool rather than a social network.
VsScenic.whenToChooseCompetitor: Pick Scenic if you're already committed to the Apple ecosystem, route planning is the single biggest thing you want from a motorcycle app, and you'd rather pay once than subscribe. Scenic's curvy-road algorithm, offline map packs, waypoint editing, and Apple Watch companion are genuinely best-in-class for solo iOS riders who don't need maintenance tracking, expense analytics, or AI diagnostics. It's also the right answer if you want to support a respected indie developer with a one-time purchase instead of a recurring bill.
VsScenic.quickVerdict: These apps barely overlap. Scenic is a gorgeous iOS-only route planner; MotoVault is a cross-platform ownership companion covering maintenance, expenses, diagnostics, and learning. If you ride an iPhone, the happiest setup is usually both — Scenic for the road, MotoVault for the garage.
VsScenic.mvWin0: Cross-platform — runs on both iOS and Android, so mixed-phone riding groups aren't left out
VsScenic.mvWin1: Complete maintenance tracking with service history, mileage and time-based reminders, and parts logs
VsScenic.mvWin2: AI-powered diagnostics — snap a photo or describe symptoms and get probable causes plus repair steps
VsScenic.mvWin3: Flexible subscription with a free tier and a 7-day Pro trial, so you can evaluate before paying
VsScenic.rvWin0: Best-in-class curvy-road routing algorithm built specifically for motorcyclists who chase twisties
VsScenic.rvWin1: Robust offline map packs that keep working deep in dead-zone touring territory
VsScenic.rvWin2: Polished Apple Watch companion with turn-by-turn directions on the wrist
VsScenic.rvWin3: Refreshing one-time purchase model — no subscription, no recurring charge
VsScenic.pricing: Scenic uses a subscription-free model: roughly $14.99 as a one-time App Store purchase, with optional in-app map packs for specific regions. MotoVault is free for core features with Pro at $4.99/month or $39.99/year — which gets you AI diagnostics, unlimited analytics, and every Pro feature on both iOS and Android. If you hate subscriptions and only need route planning on iPhone, Scenic's pricing is genuinely unbeatable.
VsScenic.verdict: Honestly, these apps barely overlap — there's no real head-to-head winner. Scenic is a lovingly built indie iOS app that does route planning better than most full teams manage. MotoVault handles everything Scenic doesn't: maintenance, expenses, diagnostics, learning, and the Android half of the rider world. If you own an iPhone, just use both. If you ride Android, MotoVault is the only one of the two you can actually install — and its maintenance and diagnostics features stand on their own either way.

0.question: Does Scenic work on Android?
0.answer: No. Scenic is iOS-only and the developer has not announced an Android version. If you're on Android and want curvy-road route planning plus maintenance tracking, MotoVault is the cross-platform option — it runs on both iOS and Android and covers the ownership side Scenic doesn't touch.

1.question: Can MotoVault replace Scenic?
1.answer: Not entirely for iOS riders who live for Scenic's curvy-road algorithm and Apple Watch turn-by-turn. What MotoVault does replace is every other motorcycle app you might pair with Scenic — maintenance tracking, service reminders, expense analytics, AI diagnostics, and learning content all live in one place, on both iOS and Android.

2.question: Is Scenic's one-time price worth it?
2.answer: If you're an iPhone rider who mainly wants curvy-road routing and offline maps, yes — around $14.99 one-time with optional map-pack IAPs is excellent value compared to yearly subscriptions. You'll still want something like MotoVault on the side for maintenance, expenses, and diagnostics, which are entirely outside Scenic's scope.

3.question: Which has better offline maps?
3.answer: Scenic does, clearly. Its regional offline map packs are a core feature and hold up well in dead-zone touring. MotoVault's offline support is partial today — good enough for logged rides and saved routes, but not yet on Scenic's level for dedicated offline navigation.

VsMotoScan.title: MotoVault vs MotoScan: AI Diagnostics (No Hardware) vs OBD Dongle Reader (2026)
VsMotoScan.description: MotoVault vs MotoScan — AI-powered motorcycle diagnostics that work on any bike with no hardware vs MotoScan's dealer-level OBD dongle reader. See which you need.
VsMotoScan.heroSubtitle: MotoVault is software-only AI diagnostics that work on any motorcycle without extra hardware. MotoScan is a hardware-based ECU reader that pairs with a dedicated OBD dongle — fundamentally different tools for different jobs.
VsMotoScan.testingPreamble: Tested April 2026 side-by-side on a BMW R1250GS with a MotoScan adapter plugged into the diagnostic port. We used MotoScan to pull real stored fault codes, live sensor streams, and battery health data. In parallel, we ran MotoVault's AI diagnostics to describe symptoms and snap photos of the bike. Both apps have legitimate, non-overlapping roles — one reads the ECU directly, the other reasons about the bike from outside.
VsMotoScan.pricingRow0Notes: MotoScan's app is free, but it does nothing without the paid hardware adapter.
VsMotoScan.pricingRow1Notes: MotoScan's cost is the dongle itself — a one-time hardware purchase, not a subscription.
VsMotoScan.pricingRow2Notes: You can't meaningfully try MotoScan without buying the adapter first.
VsMotoScan.parityRow0Mv: Yes — Claude vision + text, works on any bike
VsMotoScan.parityRow0Notes: MotoVault's biggest edge — no dongle, no supported-bike list.
VsMotoScan.parityRow1Notes: MotoScan's core strength — genuine ECU access via the adapter.
VsMotoScan.parityRow2Notes: MotoScan can clear the dash light after a fix; MotoVault cannot.
VsMotoScan.parityRow3Notes: MotoScan reads temps, pressures, and O2 sensors live from the bike.
VsMotoScan.parityRow4Notes: MotoScan reports live battery voltage via the adapter.
VsMotoScan.parityRow5Notes: MotoScan doesn't log service history or intervals.
VsMotoScan.parityRow6Mv: Yes — category breakdowns and yearly trends
VsMotoScan.parityRow7Notes: MotoScan is a pure diagnostic utility, not educational.
VsMotoScan.parityRow8Notes: MotoScan coverage depends on the adapter and supported bike list.
VsMotoScan.parityRow9Notes: MotoScan is diagnostics-only — no ride or trip features.
VsMotoScan.whenToChooseCompetitor: Pick MotoScan if you own a supported BMW, KTM, Kawasaki, or Ducati and want to read real stored ECU fault codes, clear the service warning after a DIY repair, or watch live sensor streams while you troubleshoot. Its hardware-level access is genuinely dealer-grade on covered bikes and has no software-only equivalent. We'd also recommend it to riders who already know the specific symptom they're chasing and need to confirm it against actual ECU data — that's the depth only a physical OBD connection can give you.
VsMotoScan.quickVerdict: MotoScan reads your ECU directly through a paid hardware dongle — MotoVault reasons about your bike from outside using AI and photos, with no hardware required. They solve different problems, and the best riders use both.
VsMotoScan.mvWin0: AI diagnostics that work on any motorcycle — no hardware dongle, no supported-bike list
VsMotoScan.mvWin1: Complete maintenance tracking with service history, mileage and time-based reminders
VsMotoScan.mvWin2: Photo-based symptom analysis — snap a picture of a leak, wear, or damage and get probable causes
VsMotoScan.mvWin3: Expense tracking and structured learning paths alongside diagnostics in one app
VsMotoScan.rvWin0: Reads real stored ECU fault codes directly from the bike's diagnostic port
VsMotoScan.rvWin1: Clears and resets fault codes after a DIY repair — turns the service light off
VsMotoScan.rvWin2: Live sensor data streams: coolant temp, O2 readings, fuel pressure, RPM telemetry
VsMotoScan.rvWin3: Real-time battery voltage and charging system monitoring via the adapter
VsMotoScan.pricing: MotoScan's app is free, but the MotoScan hardware adapter costs roughly $100–$150 upfront — a one-time purchase. MotoVault is free for core features with Pro from $4.99/month or $39.99/year. Over a year, pricing is comparable, but MotoScan is a hardware commitment tied to specific bike brands, while MotoVault is software that works on any motorcycle.
VsMotoScan.verdict: These are complementary tools, not competitors. MotoScan gives you genuine hardware-level ECU reads on supported BMW, KTM, Kawasaki, and Ducati bikes — nothing else does that from a consumer app. MotoVault gives you AI symptom diagnosis, maintenance tracking, expense analytics, and learning content on any motorcycle with no hardware. Serious wrenchers on supported bikes will want both: MotoScan for the bike's own voice, MotoVault for everything around it.

0.question: Does MotoVault replace an OBD scanner?
0.answer: No, and it doesn't try to. MotoVault uses AI to reason about symptoms, photos, and descriptions — it never reads your ECU directly. If you need real stored fault codes, live sensor data, or the ability to clear the service light, you still need an OBD tool like MotoScan. MotoVault is for everything around that: maintenance history, expenses, photo-based diagnosis, and learning.

1.question: Does MotoScan work on my bike?
1.answer: MotoScan supports specific models from BMW, KTM, Kawasaki, and Ducati, and coverage depends on the exact adapter variant and model year. Check MotoScan's official supported-bike list before buying the hardware. If your motorcycle isn't supported — or you ride a brand MotoScan doesn't cover — MotoVault's AI diagnostics work on any bike with no compatibility list.

2.question: Can I use both apps together?
2.answer: Yes, and it's the setup we'd recommend for serious DIY mechanics on a supported bike. Use MotoScan to pull real ECU data, read fault codes, and clear warnings after a repair. Use MotoVault to log the service history, track the expense, diagnose symptoms that don't throw a code, and learn the why behind each fix. They don't overlap at all.

3.question: Is the MotoScan adapter worth the cost?
3.answer: If you own a supported BMW, KTM, Kawasaki, or Ducati and do your own wrenching, yes — $100–$150 for dealer-level ECU access is a genuine bargain compared to a shop scan-tool session. If your bike isn't supported, if you're not comfortable clearing codes yourself, or if you mostly want maintenance tracking and symptom help, skip the hardware and start with MotoVault's AI diagnostics.

VsCalimoto.title: MotoVault vs Calimoto: AI Diagnostics vs Curvy-Road Navigation (2026)
VsCalimoto.description: MotoVault vs Calimoto — all-in-one maintenance and diagnostics app vs dedicated curvy-road navigation. Full feature comparison, pricing, and recommendations.
VsCalimoto.heroSubtitle: MotoVault is an all-in-one motorcycle platform with AI diagnostics. Calimoto is the curvy-road navigation specialist. They don't overlap much — here's the full picture.
VsCalimoto.testingPreamble: Tested April 2026 on iOS 18.3 and Android 15. MotoVault version 1.4.x, Calimoto as of its April 2026 builds on both stores. We ran Calimoto for a week of Alpine day rides while logging fuel, service, and expenses in MotoVault — then forced each app to cover the other's territory to find where the seams showed. FeaturesTripPlanning.title: Motorcycle Trip Planner — Multi-Day Route Builder & Itinerary
FeaturesTripPlanning.description: MotoVault's motorcycle trip planner app builds multi-day routes with typed waypoints (fuel, food, hotels, passes, ferries), real road routing, and rider RSVPs. Offline-capable on iOS and Android.
FeaturesTripPlanning.heroTitle: Plan Every Mile of the Ride
FeaturesTripPlanning.heroSubtitle: Multi-day routes, typed waypoints, real road routing, and a map that moves with you. The first feature we built — and the one that still shapes the rest of MotoVault.
FeaturesTripPlanning.seoHeading: Motorcycle Trip Planner for Multi-Day Routes
FeaturesTripPlanning.seoIntro: MotoVault is a motorcycle trip planning app for multi-day tours. Build a route in minutes with typed waypoints — fuel, food, scenic stops, overnights, passes, ferries — on a live map with real motorcycle-friendly road routing. Invite riders, share the link, and ride offline-capable on iOS and Android.
FeaturesTripPlanning.stat2Label: Stops per day before the itinerary gets crowded
FeaturesTripPlanning.positioningBody: Every rider we talked to had the same problem: planning a real motorcycle trip means juggling five apps. Google Maps for roads, a notes app for stops, a weather app for the pass, a messaging thread for friends, a spreadsheet for fuel budgets. It's friction every step of the way. Trip planning was the first feature we shipped because it's the feature most riders need — and because if we could nail this, everything else about MotoVault would follow from it.
FeaturesTripPlanning.howItWorksTitle: From empty map to saved ride in four steps
FeaturesTripPlanning.step1Desc: Tap the + button in Discover and a full-screen dark map opens, ready for your next adventure. Long-press anywhere to drop a stop, or search for a city, pass, coffee spot or fuel station.
FeaturesTripPlanning.step2Title: Add typed waypoints along the route
FeaturesTripPlanning.step2Desc: Each stop is more than a pin. Choose from 11 types — start, end, fuel, food, scenic, overnight, photo, mechanical, ferry, pass summit, rally point — and add notes. The stepper groups waypoints by day automatically.
FeaturesTripPlanning.step3Title: Name the ride, pick the vibe
FeaturesTripPlanning.step3Desc: Title, description, start and end dates, difficulty (Easy, Moderate, Challenging, Expert), max riders, and visibility (Private, Unlisted, Public). Every field is optional at first — you can come back and polish before publishing.
FeaturesTripPlanning.step4Title: Keep it as a draft or share the link
FeaturesTripPlanning.step4Desc: Save as a draft to keep iterating. Publish to open invites to friends, or make it public so the community can discover and join your ride. Drafts live in your My Trips, only visible to you.
FeaturesTripPlanning.galleryBody: This is an actual trip built with MotoVault: Bolzano → Passo Sella → Cortina d'Ampezzo → Passo Pordoi → Canazei → Ortisei → Passo Gardena → Bolzano. Eight typed waypoints, three days, rendered on a live map with real road routing. Every screenshot below is taken from the production app.
FeaturesTripPlanning.featuresTitle: The details that make a real trip work
FeaturesTripPlanning.f1Desc: Group waypoints by day. Day 1: Bolzano to Cortina. Day 2: the big passes. Day 3: head home. The app knows which stops belong to which day.
FeaturesTripPlanning.f2Desc: Start, end, fuel, food, scenic, overnight, photo, mechanical, ferry, pass summit, rally point — each with its own icon on the map and in the itinerary list.
FeaturesTripPlanning.f3Desc: Mapbox Directions computes the actual motorcycle-friendly route between stops. No straight-line approximations — real tarmac, real mileage.
FeaturesTripPlanning.f4Desc: Three visibility levels. Private means only you. Unlisted means anyone with the link. Public means discoverable in the Discover feed.
FeaturesTripPlanning.f5Desc: Organiser invites specific riders, or opens a public trip up to a cap. Each rider can RSVP Going, Maybe or Declined — and pick which bike they're bringing.
FeaturesTripPlanning.f6Desc: Save half-finished trips as drafts. Only you see them. Come back, add the last three stops, then publish when you're ready to share.
FeaturesTripPlanning.f7Desc: Easy, Moderate, Challenging, Expert. So nobody joins an expert pass route thinking it's a Sunday cruise.
FeaturesTripPlanning.f8Desc: Every published trip has a canonical URL. Send it to a group chat, post it to Discord, tweet it — it renders with the route as a preview.
FeaturesTripPlanning.walkthroughTitle: The story of a trip, from idea to ink
FeaturesTripPlanning.walkthroughP1: A rider wakes up on Saturday and thinks about the long weekend coming up. Three days free, bike in the garage, and a rough idea — "the Dolomites, maybe". They open MotoVault, tap Discover, then + to plan a new trip. A dark map opens to their current location.
FeaturesTripPlanning.walkthroughP2: They zoom into Bolzano and long-press to drop a Start waypoint — "Bolzano — Start, gear check & coffee before departure". Then they search Passo Sella and tap the result — it drops as a Scenic stop with the note "Iconic Dolomite pass, photo stop". They keep going: Cortina d'Ampezzo as Overnight, Passo Pordoi as Pass Summit, Canazei as Fuel, Ortisei as Overnight, Passo Gardena as Scenic, Bolzano as End. The app groups them into Day 1, Day 2, Day 3 automatically.
FeaturesTripPlanning.walkthroughP3: They name it — "Dolomites Loop — 3 Days" — write a description, pick Moderate difficulty, set max riders to 8, and leave visibility as Private. Save as draft. They go back to their garden for coffee. Later that evening they remember a better overnight in Ortisei, swap it in, toggle visibility to Public, and hit Publish. The trip is now live on Discover; two riding friends join by the end of the night.
FeaturesTripPlanning.walkthroughP4: That's the whole arc — from blank map to joined trip — and it runs on real Mapbox routing, real Postgres rows, and a bottom sheet that slides up to show the itinerary without losing the map. No spreadsheets, no screenshot chains, no lost pins.
FeaturesTripPlanning.faq0Question: Does the app actually route on real roads, or does it draw straight lines?
FeaturesTripPlanning.faq0Answer: Real roads. Between any two waypoints, we call Mapbox Directions with motorcycle-friendly routing and render the actual polyline you would ride. Zoom in on any segment of the Dolomites Loop above — you can see the hairpins.
FeaturesTripPlanning.faq1Question: Can I plan a trip before I invite anyone?
FeaturesTripPlanning.faq1Answer: Yes. Every trip starts as a draft, visible only to you. You can build and edit it across multiple sessions, and only publish when you are ready to share.
FeaturesTripPlanning.faq2Question: What happens if I invite people and only half of them can make it?
FeaturesTripPlanning.faq2Answer: Each rider RSVPs Going, Maybe or Declined, and picks which bike they are bringing. You see the count in the trip header (for example, 0/8 riders) and the full list of participants below.
FeaturesTripPlanning.faq3Question: Can I plan a trip that covers multiple countries or crossings?
FeaturesTripPlanning.faq3Answer: Yes. There are no borders in the map — add a Ferry waypoint for a Mediterranean crossing or a Pass Summit for a mountain crossing. The routing engine handles anything Mapbox can route.
FeaturesTripPlanning.faq4Question: How many waypoints can one trip have?
FeaturesTripPlanning.faq4Answer: There's no hard cap you would hit in normal use. The real constraint is readability — past 15 or 16 stops on a single day the itinerary gets busy. Split into multiple days to keep it clean.
FeaturesTripPlanning.faq5Question: Can I export the trip to another app?
FeaturesTripPlanning.faq5Answer: Every published trip has a canonical URL with a route preview. You can also share from the trip detail screen; native share lets you paste it into Messages, Slack, Discord, or your notes.

FeaturesTripPlanning.ctaBody: Trip planning is the founding feature of MotoVault. Download the app, drop your first waypoint, and see why we built it before anything else.
